what_this_is: Real token counts for every decision prompt in the month one eval, measured against OpenRouter on 2026-09-06, plus the month one cost table computed from them. Regenerate the token counts with: agent/decide.py --measure --real

how_the_calls_were_made.spend_source: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key, field byok_usage_daily. This key routes through BYOK, so the per call 'cost' field in every chat completion came back as 0 and the real figure only shows up in the key's byok_usage counters. The ledger must not read that 0 as free.

packets_used.insider: synthetic, 15 candidates for pick and 8 open positions for manage, built by agent/decide.py
packets_used.congress: synthetic, 15 candidates for pick and 8 open positions for manage, built by agent/decide.py

measurements.note: reasoning tokens used the whole 600 token budget, so no JSON came back
the only untruncated answer of the eight: valid JSON, one action and one reason for each of 4 positions

extra_calls.why: does a low reasoning effort leave room for an answer at 600 tokens
extra_calls.call: openrouter/anthropic/claude-fable-5.1, momentum_hybrid manage, reasoning effort low
extra_calls.result: no. Even at low effort Fable used the whole 600 tokens and returned no text.

extra_calls.why: how many tokens is the system prompt on its own, which is the part caching could hold
extra_calls.call: openrouter/anthropic/claude-fable-5.1, momentum pick system prompt plus a one character user message
extra_calls.result: 2.84 characters per token for Fable on this prose

extra_calls.why: the same isolating call on the other model
extra_calls.call: openrouter/openai/gpt-6-astra, momentum pick system prompt plus a one character user message
extra_calls.result: 4.09 characters per token for Astra, so the same prompt costs Astra about 30 percent fewer tokens

system_and_user_split.how: system tokens are the character count of the rendered system prompt divided by the characters per token measured above. user tokens are the measured total minus that.

prompt_drift_since_measurement.what_happened: the prompts were rewritten after the eight calls so that every placeholder name is the exact key name in the book's strategy.yaml
prompt_drift_since_measurement.size_change: pick prompts grew 101 to 151 characters, manage prompts grew 4 to 6, which is 35 to 55 Fable tokens on a 6581 token prompt, under one percent. The cost table was not re-measured for it.

anthropic_claude_fable_5_1.how_to_turn_it_on: a cache_control breakpoint, either {'type':'ephemeral'} at the top level of the request body, or on a content block: {'type':'text','text':'...','cache_control':{'type':'ephemeral'}}
anthropic_claude_fable_5_1.minimum_note: OpenRouter's own page does not list Fable and its stated tiers are stale. 512 comes from Anthropic's current table. A prompt under the minimum is processed with no caching and no error.
anthropic_claude_fable_5_1.cache_read_note: Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 only. Every other Anthropic model is 0.1x. OpenRouter's prose still says 0.1x; its live pricing API says 0.025x and agrees with Anthropic.
anthropic_claude_fable_5_1.default_ttl: 5 minutes, extendable to 1 hour with ttl: '1h' on the breakpoint
anthropic_claude_fable_5_1.ttl_note: the clock starts when the writing request starts, not when its response ends, so a 15 second answer eats 15 seconds of a 5 minute cache
anthropic_claude_fable_5_1.breakpoint_placement: the end of the system message works and is the documented example. Caching covers tools, then system, then messages, in that order, up to the breakpoint.

openai_gpt_6_astra.cache_read_note: OpenRouter's prose says 0.25x or 0.5x, which is the GPT-4 era. Every GPT-5 and GPT-6 model computes to 0.1x and OpenAI's own guide says 0.1x.
openai_gpt_6_astra.cache_write_note: GPT-5.6 and later charge for writes even though caching is automatic
openai_gpt_6_astra.retention: 30 minutes from the last write or reuse, refreshed free on reuse
openai_gpt_6_astra.prefix_matching: strict. The whole rendered prefix has to match, and response_format counts as part of it, so changing the JSON schema busts the cache.

how_openrouter_reports_it.usage.prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_: tokens written, only on models with paid writes
how_openrouter_reports_it.cache_discount: not in the chat response, only on the /api/v1/generation metadata endpoint
how_openrouter_reports_it.usage_include_true: deprecated and ignored, usage is always returned now

caching_rules_checked_2026_09_06.routing: OpenRouter keeps a sticky session to the provider that holds the cache for 10 minutes, unless provider.order is set by hand, which turns stickiness off. Pass a session_id to make stickiness reliable for a loop whose messages keep changing.
